messages:
Maria: heads-up ran a replay vs synth bench to isolate why kernel picking deviates during region drain. attaching quick notes + logs.

Kevin: nice — does that include the kv priming step?

Maria: yes. setup: replay the exact prod trace for endpoint /generate (prefixes included) to reproduce kv hit skew, then run a synthetic Poisson/steady workload to compare.

Maria: command I used:
```
./bench-run --mode=replay --trace=prod_2026-02-14.trace --regions=us-east1,us-west1 --concurrency=40 --duration=600 \
  --fallback-policy=regional-prefer --fallback-model=redwood-compact-8q --warmup-prefixes=1000
```

Maria: and for the synthetic run:
```
./bench-run --mode=synth --dist=poisson --lambda=30 --seq-dist=prod-seq-hist.json --regions=us-east1,us-west1 --duration=600
```

Jonathan: how did you ensure the KV cache state matched between runs? that's usually the tricky bit for apples-to-apples.

Maria: good call — we added an explicit "kv_prime" step that replays the first N requests from the trace before measurement window. N=1000 in this case. also pinned random seeds and disabled async eviction during measurement.

Sasha: sharing profiler output for the replay run (trimmed):
```
Top hotspots (replay, us-east1):
  batching_dispatch                  12.3%
  kernel_selection                  8.9%
  kv_cache_lock                     4.7%
  io_serialization                  3.1%
  decoder_kernel                    27.6%
```
Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/1876543210 (internal)

bench-bot: summary: replay vs synth p95/p99 divergence detected across region failover scenarios:
```
us-east1 (replay): p50=19ms p95=110ms p99=260ms
us-west1 (replay): p50=23ms p95=140ms p99=310ms
us-east1 (synth): p50=17ms p95=95ms p99=180ms
failover to us-west1 (replay with fallback-model compact): p50=35ms p95=220ms p99=480ms
```

Maria: tl;dr: when KV hit-rate drops in replay during drain, our kernel selection heuristic (recent change to prefer compact kernels for quantized models) picks a kernel variant with slightly different memory/read patterns that increases tail latency under cache-miss-heavy sequences. synth workload didn't expose it because hit-rate stayed high.

Kevin: interesting — so it's a selection *policy* regression, not a GPU kernel bug. can we force the old heuristic for now?

Maria: yes — two short-term mitigations:
  1) revert the heuristic change in the policy table for redwood-compact-8q (canary in us-west1).
  2) widen batching window by 5ms for fallback routes to amortize kernel switch overhead while cache warming happens.

Sasha: would widening batching affect tail for low-latency customers? we should gate by customer tier.

Maria: agreed, only enable widened-window for "dedicated-fallback" policy during failover; leave host-tier unchanged.

Jonathan: what's the recommended apples-to-apples checklist for future runs? can we codify it in the bench harness?

Maria: proposed checklist (to add to docs/runbooks):
  - pin seeds and deterministic scheduling flags
  - run kv_prime with N identical to real prefix length
  - capture pre-measurement KV hit-rate and miss-rate snapshots
  - run synth using extracted seq-length and temperature distributions from trace
  - run both replay and synth under identical region-routing/fallback config
  - store kernel-selection logs (kernel_id sequence) for postmortem

Kevin: I'll open a perf ticket and kick off a canary revert + widened-window run. tagging @Jonathan and @Sasha for infra and SLO review.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-2026-1893: "kernel-selection tail regression during region failover" assigned to Kevin — https://issue.redwood/INF-2026-1893

bench-bot: scheduling canary runs now (us-west1 only) — will post results as thread updates :hourglass: 

Maria: thanks all. if the canary looks good we'll roll to other regions and follow up with a short postmortem + decision (revert vs refine heuristic). :thumbsup:
